SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 7-day history of fever with alternating chills and sweats, generalized myalgia, nausea with poor oral intake, marked fatigue, and night sweats.
- Associated negatives: No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, new or severe headache, rash, joint swelling, dysuria, urinary frequency.
- Travel history: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; rural trekking, cycling, river/beach exposure. Took daily malaria prophylaxis (exact drug unknown; possibly two different tablets).
- Past medical history: Chronic mechanical/postural back pain (under physiotherapy). Episodic screen-related headaches. No other significant illnesses reported.
- Medications:
  • Seroxat (paroxetine) – dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • Ibuprofen – OTC, “recommended dose”  
  • Paracetamol – OTC, “recommended dose”
- Social history: Works as a nurse. Non-smoker. Moderate alcohol intake. Performs moderate exercise a few times per week.
- Allergies: Seasonal pollen (hay fever). Denies drug allergies.
- Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction at age 68.

Objective:
- No physical examination performed during teleconsultation.
- No vital signs documented.
- No investigations performed yet.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Pyrexia of unknown origin post-travel
   - Assessment: Suspected infectious etiology; malaria or other tropical infection high on list.
   - Differential diagnosis: Malaria, dengue, typhoid, viral illness, bacterial infection, inflammatory condition.
   - Investigations planned:
     • In-person physical examination  
     • Blood tests: thick & thin blood films for malaria, full blood count, inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR), liver/renal function, blood cultures as indicated.  
   - Treatment planned:
     • Continue antipyretics (paracetamol/ibuprofen) as needed.  
     • Off work until evaluation completed.  
   - Referrals:
     • Same-day appointment at central clinic for examination and phlebotomy.  
     • If unable to attend, advised to present to local A&E with clinician’s note.

2. Chronic mechanical back pain
   - Assessment: Ongoing postural/mechanical back pain.
   - Treatment planned: Continues current physiotherapy program; no additional intervention discussed today.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No vital signs, physical examination findings, or medication dosages documented; vaccination and full drug allergy review not detailed.  
● No internal transcript conflicts identified.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor background noise but clinical content intelligible.
